items.title: Complete symmetrized constant-coefficient evolution
items.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $m\ge1$, let $U:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^m$, and let $A_1,A_2,A_3,B,M\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$ be constant matrices. Assume $M=M^{\mathsf T}$ is positive definite, each $MA_j$ is symmetric, and $S:=(MB+B^{\mathsf T}M)/2$ is positive semidefinite. Consider

$$\partial_tU+\sum_{j=1}^3A_j\partial_{x_j}U+BU=0.$$

For $U_0\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^m)$ there is a unique global smooth solution, Schwartz in $x$ at each time and continuous in every Schwartz seminorm on compact time intervals. With the negative-sign, $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform, put $\widehat U(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}U(x)\,dx$ and define, for $s\ge0$,

$$\|U\|_{H^s_M}^2:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}(1+|\xi|^2)^s\widehat U(\xi)^*M\widehat U(\xi)\,d\xi.$$

For $t\ge0$, $\|U(t)\|_{H^s_M}\le\|U_0\|_{H^s_M}$ for every $s\ge0$; hence the solution depends continuously on the data in each such norm. The same conclusions hold for smooth periodic data on the flat torus $\mathbb T_L^3:=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$, $L>0$, with Fourier coefficients $\widehat U_k=L^{-3}\int_{[0,L]^3}U(x)e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x/L}\,dx$ and

$$\|U\|_{H^s_M(\mathbb T_L^3)}^2:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k/L|^2)^s\widehat U_k^*M\widehat U_k.$$

For periodic data, $\|U(t)\|_\infty\le C_{s,L,M}\|U_0\|_{H^s_M(\mathbb T_L^3)}$ for each integer $s>3/2$.

For a unit vector $\nu\in\mathbb R^3$, write $A(\nu)=\sum_j\nu_jA_j$ and $\widetilde A(\nu)=M^{1/2}A(\nu)M^{-1/2}$. The finite speed

$$v_*:=\sup_{|\nu|=1}\max\{|\lambda|:\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(\widetilde A(\nu))\}$$

is finite. If $v_*>0$, $R>v_*t$, and $U_0$ vanishes on $B_R(x_0)$, then $U(t)$ vanishes on $B_{R-v_*t}(x_0)$ for $0\le t<R/v_*$. The same assertion holds on $\mathbb T_L^3$ using its geodesic distance. If $v_*=0$, every $A_j=0$ and the system is a pointwise linear ODE, so spatial support does not move. These are conclusions for the displayed linear systems; no variable-coefficient or nonlinear existence claim is included.

items.title: Perfect sound characteristic and actual stable causal linear branch
items.statement:
Let $c>0$ be a fixed speed parameter, use Minkowski coordinates $x^0=ct$ with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and consider a smooth perfect-fluid state at a uniform rest point. The local state has energy per marker $e\in C^2(X)$ on an open domain $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, with specific volume $v=1/n$ and specific entropy $\sigma_p$; $e_{vv}$ denotes the second derivative at fixed $\sigma_p$. At the rest point assume $n_0>0$, $T_0>0$, $h_0=\epsilon_0+p_0>0$, and $e_{vv}>0$. Let

$$a_s:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\epsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}}{n_0h_0},$$

as in [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]], and assume additionally $a_s\le1$. For adiabatic perturbations $\delta\sigma_p=0$, write $r=\delta\epsilon$ and $w=\delta u_{\rm spatial}\in\mathbb R^3$. The linearized equations obtained from the no-force perfect stress and particle balances of [[lem-tgr-perfect-fluid-projection]] are

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c a_s}{h_0}\nabla r=0.$$

For Schwartz data on $\mathbb R^3$ or smooth periodic data on $\mathbb T_L^3$, these equations have the unique global smooth solution supplied by [[lem-tgr-constant-linear-energy-causality]]. The positive quadratic energy density $\mathcal E=\tfrac12[(a_s/h_0)r^2+h_0|w|^2]$ has flux $c a_s r w$, and the solution is contractive in the corresponding weighted $L^2$ and Sobolev norms. Its characteristic speeds are $0$ and $\pm c\sqrt{a_s}$; for positive $a_s$, this cone lies inside the reference cone of speed $c$ exactly when $a_s\le1$. These are statements about this frozen linear system only; they do not assert a nonlinear or curved-spacetime evolution theorem.

For the formal coefficient comparison in [A3], if the same linear equations are assigned $a_s>1$, their plane-wave speed is $c\sqrt{a_s}>c$. If they are assigned $a_s<0$, smooth periodic modes grow as $e^{c\sqrt{-a_s}|k|t}$ at arbitrarily large wave numbers. The case $a_s=0$ is degenerate: the displayed positive energy matrix is no longer positive definite, so the stability proof above does not apply.

items.title: Corrected bulk relaxation and exact extended entropy
items.statement:
Use the smooth $(-,+,+,+)$ Lorentzian data, local state, and conventions of [[lem-tgr-perfect-fluid-projection]] and [[lem-tgr-dissipative-entropy-identity]], with $n>0$, $T>0$, $c>0$, $x^0=ct$, and smooth future unit $u$. Assume positive $C^1$ coefficients $\zeta$ and $\tau$, set $\beta=\tau/\zeta$, and let $\Pi$ be a smooth scalar. In the bulk-only branch take

$$T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a,\qquad \nabla_aT^{ab}=0,\qquad \nabla_aJ^a=0,$$

where $\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, $\theta=\nabla_au^a$, and $a^b_{\rm acc}=Du^b$. Adopt the corrected relaxation law

$$\beta D\Pi+\frac{\Pi}{\zeta c}=-\theta-\frac{T\Pi}{2}\nabla_a\!\left(\frac{\beta u^a}{T}\right)$$

and the extended entropy current $S^a=[s-\beta\Pi^2/(2T)]u^a$. Then the stress and particle equations imply

$$D\epsilon+(h+\Pi)\theta=0,\qquad (h+\Pi)a^b_{\rm acc}+\Delta^{ba}\nabla_a(p+\Pi)=0,\qquad Dn+n\theta=0,$$

and every actual smooth solution of the stated corrected law satisfies

$$\nabla_aS^a=\frac{\Pi^2}{\zeta cT}\ge0.$$

Here $\beta$ has units $\mathrm{Pa^{-1}}$, $\Pi,\epsilon,p,h$ have units Pa, $D,\theta,a_{\rm acc}$ have inverse-length components, and the correction $\beta\Pi^2/(2T)$ has the units of entropy density. The law is an explicit model assumption; dropping its derivative term does not yield the stated sign identity in general.

There is an exact homogeneous solution on Minkowski space: for constant state, $u=(1,0,0,0)$, constant positive $\zeta,\tau,T$, and $\Pi(t)=\Pi_0e^{-t/\tau}$, the stress and particle balances and the corrected law hold, with strict entropy production wherever $\Pi(t)\ne0$. This witness is not a general nonlinear existence theorem.

items.title: Bulk linear relaxation energy, stability and causal speed
items.statement:
Use the uniform Minkowski rest equilibrium of the bulk-only model of [[lem-tgr-bulk-relaxation-entropy]], with constant background state $(n_0,\epsilon_0,p_0,T_0,\sigma_{p0})$, velocity $u_0=(1,0,0,0)$, and bulk pressure $\Pi_0=0$. Set $h_0:=\epsilon_0+p_0$ and assume $n_0,T_0,h_0,e_{vv},c>0$. The local state has specific energy $e\in C^2(X)$ on an open domain, with specific volume $v=1/n$ and specific entropy $\sigma_p$; $e_{vv}$ is evaluated at fixed $\sigma_p$. Take constant coefficients $\zeta,\tau>0$ and adiabatic perturbations $\delta\sigma_p=0$. Let

$$a_s:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\epsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}}{n_0h_0}>0$$

as supplied by [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]]. Write $r=\delta\epsilon$, $w=\delta u_{\rm spatial}$, and denote the first-order perturbation $\delta\Pi$ by $\Pi$ in the linearized equations. The system is

$$r_t+c h_0\operatorname{div}w=0,\qquad w_t+\frac{c}{h_0}\nabla(a_s r+\Pi)=0,\qquad \tau\Pi_t+\Pi=-\zeta c\operatorname{div}w.$$

Its positive quadratic energy density

$$\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}=\frac12\left[\frac{a_s}{h_0}r^2+h_0|w|^2+\frac{\tau}{\zeta}\Pi^2\right]$$

satisfies $\partial_t\mathcal E_{\rm bulk}+\operatorname{div}[c(a_s r+\Pi)w]=-\Pi^2/\zeta$. The normal characteristic speeds are $0$ and $\pm v_{\rm bulk}$, where

$$v_{\rm bulk}=c\sqrt{a_s+\frac{\zeta}{\tau h_0}}.$$

By [[lem-tgr-constant-linear-energy-causality]], Schwartz data on $\mathbb R^3$ and smooth periodic data on $\mathbb T_L^3$ have unique global smooth solutions, contractive in the corresponding energy and Sobolev norms, with finite propagation at $v_{\rm bulk}$. The branch is inside the reference speed $c$ exactly when $a_s+\zeta/(\tau h_0)\le1$. Constant density and transverse velocity modes can persist, so contraction does not mean every mode decays. No nonlinear or variable-coefficient existence theorem is claimed.

items.title: Positive relaxation parameters can give superluminal characteristic speed
items.statement: In the bulk linear branch of [[lem-tgr-bulk-linear-causality]], choose any $h_0>0$ and $\tau>0$, set $\zeta=\tau h_0$, and take $a_s=1/3$. Then every parameter is positive, but the exact normal characteristic speed is $2c/\sqrt3>c$. This is a parameterized mathematical example, not a measurement or an estimate for a material.
